hook.hook: Nobody tells you what to do with a glut of Brussels sprouts

captions.instagram:
Nobody tells you what to do with a glut of Brussels sprouts

If you are wondering what to do with a glut of Brussels sprouts, I recommend roasting them. I roast mine with olive oil and balsamic vinegar for a caramelised flavour, or make Crispy Roast Brussels Sprouts. You can also boil or steam whole sprouts for six to eight minutes so nothing goes to waste.

Check your local frost dates.

hook.hook: Nobody tells you November is still garlic planting time

captions.instagram:
Nobody tells you November is still garlic planting time

I get asked all the time how to grow garlic in the UK without it rotting in the ground. Plant the biggest cloves in well drained soil and let them sit through the cold months until summer. You will get a proper harvest for cooking with hardly any effort.

Do not store raw garlic in oil at room temperature, as there is a risk of botulism.

Check your local frost dates.

hook.hook: 2 simple ways to cook surplus lettuce before it spoils.

captions.instagram:
2 simple ways to cook surplus lettuce before it spoils.

If you are wondering what to do with a glut of lettuce, do not let it go to waste. You can lightly cook outer leaves in soups with peas or braise gem and cos hearts in butter and stock. Cooked soup can even be frozen in portions for up to 6 months, though raw leaves cannot be frozen.

Check your local frost dates.
